# M3-14a: Slack and alerts in serve

- Milestone: M3
- Branch / worktree: `t/M3-14a`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M3-14a`
- Depends on: M3-5, M3-10b, M3-12a
- Touches (exclusive while running): cmd/, config/
- Plan refs: §5 startup self-check, R11a, N2; STATE M1-4b (shutdown wait)
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no (smoke: none; ships in M3-17)

## Goal
`finbot serve` runs the Socket Mode client and sends freshness alerts after each sync, and shutdown can no longer hang.

## Scope
- Config: `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, `SLACK_USERS` (`<name>:<slack id>,...`; the main .env holds `brendan:…,hilarie:…`), upserted into `users` at start. Socket Mode is off unless both and `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` are set. Errors name the variable, never the value. `SLACK_USERS` is already in the main `.env` (2 humans, set by sup): sup confirms, unprinted, that it has this shape before this task's tests use it, or tells the builder its shape.
- Add `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` and each Slack user id from `SLACK_USERS` to `secrets(cfg)` in `cmd/app.go`.
- Start the client under the serve ctx. A self-check failure raises a critical alert and is logged; the mirror keeps syncing.
- After each scheduled sync, feed `alerts/`. Outcomes never fail the sync job or touch `Health`.
- Bounded shutdown: every wait on shutdown (scheduler job, socket client, HTTP servers) shares a deadline. On expiry, log and exit, so a hung job can't hold the process.

## Out of scope
- The categorize job and `CLASSIFY_MODE` (M3-14b). Import status (M3-15). `deploy.sh` forwards (M3-17).

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Config tests: all set, one missing (feature off), malformed `SLACK_USERS` names the variable and not the value.
- [ ] Test: the app token and both Slack user ids are scrubbed by the log redaction.
- [ ] Test: a job that ignores ctx doesn't stop `serve` from returning within the deadline.
- [ ] Test: an alert failure leaves the sync successful and `Health` unchanged.
- [ ] Test: a self-check failure sends a critical alert and sync continues.
- [ ] go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `config/`: `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` (must start `xapp-`) and `SLACK_USERS` (`<name>:<U…|W…>,...`; names brendan→`brendan`, hilarie or wife→`wife`, each label and id once). `Config.SocketMode()` is true only with app token, bot token and users all set; `Config.SlackIDs()`. Errors name the variable, never the value.
  - `cmd/slack.go` (new): `startSlack` upserts users, builds the client (`newSocketClient`, injectable), runs the self-check once before the first sync (20 s cap), then runs the client on its own goroutine. A failed self-check is logged and sends the critical `socket_self_check` alert (dedupe key `channel`), then retries with backoff (1 m doubling to 30 m); a pass clears that alert. A socket that stops is logged and restarted with the same backoff. Before the channel resolves, alerts post by channel name, so a broken lookup (e.g. a missing scope) can still alert. The alerter is wrapped in a mutex, since the socket goroutine sends alongside the scheduler.
  - `cmd/app.go`: after each successful (not skipped, not cancelled) scheduled sync, `feedAlerts` runs `Alerter.Freshness` (from `Syncer.Freshness`) and `Alerter.Anomalies`. Failures are only logged. The scheduler, MCP and Slack waits and the HTTP drain share one `shutdownTimeout` (5 s) deadline. Past it, serve logs `shutdown deadline passed; exiting anyway` with `waiting_on` and exits 1. `secrets()` now covers `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` and every `SLACK_USERS` id.
  - Test hook `slackBaseURL` lets serve tests point the status message at a local fake.
- Acceptance:
  - Config tests (all set, each one missing → off, malformed `SLACK_USERS`/`SLACK_APP_TOKEN` names the variable and not the value, hilarie/wife mapping): pass. `go test ./config -run 'Slack'`
  - Redaction of app token and both user ids: pass. `go test ./cmd -run TestSecrets_CoverSlack`; the serve self-check test also greps the logs for all four values.
  - Job that ignores ctx doesn't hold serve: pass. `go test ./cmd -run TestServe_HungJobDoesNotHoldShutdown` (returns in about 0.3 s, exit 1, log names `scheduler`)
  - Alert failure leaves sync OK and Health 200: pass. `go test ./cmd -run TestSyncJob_AlertFailureLeavesSyncAndHealth`
  - Self-check failure sends a critical alert (stored, posted once) and sync continues: pass. `go test ./cmd -run 'TestServe_SelfCheck'` (also checks recovery clears the alert and starts the socket, and the users are upserted)
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`: green. `go test -race ./cmd`: green on 3 runs. One earlier race run had `TestServe_SIGTERMClosesListenersAndDB` time out waiting for healthz 200; it didn't recur in 3 isolated and 2 full race runs, so I'm treating it as a load flake.
- Deviations from brief:
  - Alerts run only when Socket Mode is on (all three Slack vars set), because their poster is the Socket Mode client.
  - A deadline-expired shutdown exits 1, not 0.
- Follow-ups for backlog:
  - `slack.Handlers` are empty, so Socket Mode traffic is acked and dropped. M3-14b should wire `slack.Questions` (it needs the writer).
  - A socket that keeps failing after a good self-check (e.g. a revoked app token) is only logged, never alerted. Consider an alert.
  - The status message doesn't show the Slack self-check state.
- Docs follow-ups (CLAUDE.md):
  - Configuration: `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` (xapp-, secret) and `SLACK_USERS` (`brendan:<id>,hilarie:<id>`; names map to store labels brendan→brendan, hilarie or wife→wife; anything else is a config error). Socket Mode and alerts are off unless both Slack tokens and `SLACK_USERS` are set. The Slack user ids are scrubbed from logs like secrets.
  - Architecture/cmd: serve upserts users and runs the Slack self-check before the first sync (a failure sends the critical alert, retries with backoff, sync continues). It feeds freshness and anomaly alerts after each successful scheduled sync, and their outcome never touches `Health`. Shutdown waits share one 5 s deadline; past it serve logs and exits 1.
  - `deploy.sh` needs to forward `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` and `SLACK_USERS` (M3-17).
